subject.title: [Bug]: Gateway heap grows to 1073MB+ at idle on macOS, cron jobs fail silently under memory pressure (ref #86613, #86509)

question: Should cron failure reporting for a wedged or killed Gateway remain in-process only, or should OpenClaw add durable started-without-terminal-result recovery that can surface failure after restart?
rationale: The remaining gap spans product semantics for failure alerts, task history, and restart recovery, not only the already-fixed memory-core watcher leak.

options.title: Add Durable Recovery
options.body: Treat stale started cron runs without terminal outcomes as a recoverable failure/lost state and surface that through task history or failure alerts after restart.

options.title: Diagnostics Only
options.body: Keep memory and liveness diagnostics as the supported surface and document that failureAlert is best-effort while the Gateway process is wedged.

options.title: External Watchdog
options.body: Move this class of failure reporting to a launchd or doctor watchdog path instead of extending cron runtime semantics.

recommendation.title: Add Durable Recovery
recommendation.body: Treat stale started cron runs without terminal outcomes as a recoverable failure/lost state and surface that through task history or failure alerts after restart.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent task/session reliability history makes this the best available owner signal for the durable failure-reporting decision.
